name: Side plank
pattern: Anti-lateral-flexion hold: on one forearm and the side of the feet, the body stays straight while the bottom-side trunk muscles stop the hips dropping.
setup: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, forearm flat.
Legs straight, top foot in front of or on top of the bottom foot.
Top hand on your hip or reaching up.

steps.text: Lift your hips until your body is one straight line from head to feet, and hold. Switch sides.

cues.cue: Hips high: one straight line from head to feet.
cues.why: The side bridge challenges quadratus lumborum and the obliques with low spine load.
A stacked arm keeps the shoulder stable and comfortable.

cues.cue: Push the hips slightly forward, glutes squeezed.
cues.why: Hips drifting back turn it into a pike; glute med works hard in this hold.

cues.cue: Chest faces forward, don't roll toward the floor.
cues.why: Rolling shifts load off the side muscles.

breathing: Breathe steadily; keep a light brace.

tempo.note: Hold 10-30 s each side. In healthy adults side hold time was about 99% of the flexor test in men and 79% in women.

mistakes.name: Hips sag
mistakes.looks: The hips sink toward the floor and the body bends sideways.
mistakes.fix: Lift the bottom hip up to the line.
mistakes.why: The side muscles have let go.

mistakes.name: Hips push back
mistakes.looks: The hips sit back behind the shoulders and feet.
mistakes.fix: Push your hips forward, glutes on.
mistakes.why: Hip flexion shortens the lever and takes load off the obliques.

mistakes.name: Sinking into the shoulder
mistakes.looks: The bottom shoulder rises toward the ear.
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away with the forearm.
mistakes.why: Hanging on the shoulder strains it.

safety: Shoulder pain: start with a bent-knee side plank or with the hand on a bench.
Keep both sides balanced; big side-to-side differences are worth working on.

variants.change: Knees bent, weight on the bottom knee: easier.
On the hand with a straight arm: higher, more shoulder work.
Top leg lifts: a very high gluteus medius exercise.
Top foot on a bench, bottom leg free (Copenhagen): heavy adductor work.
Load in the top hand or a row: adds rotation demand.
Moving the top elbow or arm while holding the hips up.

subtypes.name: Bent-knee side plank
subtypes.change: Knees bent about 90 degrees; hips lift from the knee.

subtypes.name: Side plank with leg lift
subtypes.change: Top leg lifts about 30 degrees and lowers while the hips stay high.

motion.basis: Body lies on its right side (rig rolls the whole body 90 degrees); joint angles are relative to the body. Hip sag is shown as bottom-hip adduction because the convention has no trunk side-bend key. Angles are estimates; hold-time ratios from mcgill1999.
